data.rationale: 1. Control Node Catalog Scope is Well-Bounded but Miscoded: The control account 1.16.05.24 (CS_SW IFC 4.0_Fixed Control Node Target Catalog) has a clear functional boundary for managing the intermediate-level target catalogs at the Control Node. However, it is structurally misaligned within the WBS hierarchy.2. Systemic Coding Index Shift Persists Across All Database Modules: This account confirms that the +1 WBS index shift is systematically applied across all target-related databases (including Silo Target Catalog .23 and Wing-Wide Target Catalog .25). It resides under 1.16.05 (reserved for IFC 5.0 in the proposed CSDR WBS) rather than 1.16.4 (IFC 4.0 / Full Launch Capability).3. Critical Middle-Tier Database Dependencies: The Control Node Target Catalog is the vital intermediate data layer distributing targets to individual launch silos. Because of the coding misalignment, automated tools cannot correctly verify configuration dependencies between this middle-tier database and the end-point silos.

areas.text: The Government has Moderate confidence in the contractor's planning maturity for this control account. The functional planning is sound: a clear, trackable, and bounded software database product has been defined with a logical owner (CAM Tyrone Jackson). However, the systemic WBS index shift is present here as well, meaning the account structurally resides under the wrong parent capability branch. This misalignment prevents a "Strong" confidence rating because it breaks automated EVMS, CSDR, and program-level tracking.

While the technical scope of the Control Node Target Catalog is well-defined, its WBS code placement in the RAM (1.16.05.24) places it outside the government’s defined Full Launch Capability (IFC 4.0) scope (1.16.4). The contractor must map this and all associated target database accounts back to the correct parent hierarchy before the baseline is finalized.

The control account schedule sequences are internally logical and ready for loading. However, loading them under WBS 1.16.05 instead of 1.16.04 will generate direct conflicts with the proposed WBS, hindering future schedule health checks and automated schedule status reporting.

data.products: Northrop Grumman Responsibility Assignment Matrix, Government Proposed WBS (CSDR WBS - WAS_IS 2 Apr 2026), Proposed CSDR WBS Dictionary, Sentinel Statement of Work Revision 9.0
data.strengths:
Strength 1 (Consolidated Target/Catalog Domain CAM): Consolidating this account under Tyrone Jackson—who also owns the Silo Target Catalog (1.16.05.23) and Wing-Wide Target Catalog (1.16.05.25)—minimizes the risk of communication gaps and ensures a unified technical approach to database schema development.
Strength 2 (Logical Functional Boundaries): Separating the control node database from the silo database represents a clean, modular software design that aligns with open-system design principles.
data.concerns: Concern 1 (WBS Index Shift - 1.16.05 vs. 1.16.04):The contractor has coded this IFC 4.0 database account under WBS 1.16.05.24. The proposed CSDR WBS Dictionary reserves 1.16.5 for IFC 5.0. All IFC 4.0 software tasks must map to WBS 1.16.4 (Full Launch Capability).Risk 1:This structural coding mismatch breaks direct program-level cost collection, which will cause compliance and audit failures in CSDR and IPMDAR reporting by blending IFC 4.0 and IFC 5.0 database actuals.Concern 2 (Database Synchronization Failure Risks):The Control Node database must dynamically sync data downward to launch silos and upward to wing-wide controllers.Risk 2:If the database WBS lines are structurally desynchronized, delays in design updates for one database tier cannot be automatically analyzed for impact on another tier, increasing the risk of database version mismatches during HWIL test campaigns.
data.questions: Question 1: What is the technical mechanism for target data distribution between the Control Node database (.24) and individual Silo databases (.23)? Is it automated or operator-driven?Follow-Up 1: Contractor to provide the system/subsystem design description (SSDD) detailing the control node-to-silo data transaction protocols.Question 2: Will the contractor present a unified correction plan to shift the target catalog control accounts from the 1.16.05 prefix back to 1.16.04 (to map to 1.16.4)?Follow-Up 2: Contractor to provide a redlined RAM showing the corrected software mappings before baseline locking.
data.integration: Observation 1 (Middle-Tier Synchronization): The Control Node catalog sits technically between the Wing-Wide Target Catalogs (1.16.05.25) and the Fixed Launch Silo Target Catalogs (1.16.05.23). Tracing these cross-functional database schema dependencies is a major risk when the physical hardware node installations (such as Launch Center Node Integration under WBS 1.4.2.2.3) are mapped separately from the software branch.Observation 2 (Lack of Automated EVMS Linkage): The physical installation and verification of the control node processing equipment occurs under WBS 1.4.2.2.2.1 (Launch Center Integrated Assemblies). Due to the WBS indexing misalignment, automated systems cannot automatically link schedule delays in hardware to the development of this intermediate database.
